checks.name: cv_strategy_validity
checks.detail: validation_strategy.json.chosen_strategy='stratified_kfold' with stratify_column='label', n_splits=5, random_state=42. Matches data structure: no time/group/panel columns (spec_parse.json.detected_structure), balanced 3-class target (40 samples each, minority_class_rate=0.333). Holdout is val.csv (separate file, never used in training). CV correctly simulates hidden evaluation on balanced val.csv.

checks.name: cv_holdout_calibration
checks.detail: Linear specialist OOF f1_macro=0.9750 vs holdout f1_macro=0.9327 (prediction_sanity.json). Absolute gap=0.0423. Relative to floor_self_reported (0.0833): 0.0423/0.0833=50.8%, exceeding the 8% relative threshold. However, floor_self_reported=0.0833 is an artificially low baseline (1/12 of even random guessing on 3 classes); relative to proper 3-class random baseline 0.333 the gap is 12.7%. Two of 5 folds scored 1.0 (cv_fold_scores=[1.0, 1.0, 0.958, 0.958, 0.958]) indicating fold-level variance on this 120-row dataset. No cross-round trend available (round 1). Gap is consistent with small-dataset variance rather than structural leakage, but warrants monitoring if a round 2 occurs.

checks.name: prediction_sanity
checks.detail: submission.csv: 30 rows, 3 unique class labels [0,1,2], counts {0:9, 1:12, 2:9}. Coefficient of variation=0.816 (>>0.01 — non-constant). No clipping applicable (classification). All values within valid class range {0,1,2}. Class distribution roughly balanced (30/10/10/10 expected; 9/12/9 observed — minor skew to class 1 but within sampling variance). All 30 predictions finite. Corroborates prediction_sanity.json verdict=PASS.

checks.name: train_val_gap
checks.detail: Relative train-val gap: |0.9750 - 0.9327| / 0.9750 = 4.34%, well below the 30% WARN threshold. GBDT OOF f1_macro=0.9583 vs linear 0.9750; both substantially above floor. NNLS weights: linear=1.0, gbdt=0.0 — ensemble collapsed to single best model, not a blending artifact. No suspiciously near-perfect score: cv=0.9750 < 0.987 threshold (baseline 0.333 + 0.98*(1-0.333)).

checks.name: species_leakage_exclusion
checks.detail: validation_strategy.json flags species as HIGH severity leakage (direct string encoding of label). Both 20260616_004306_agent_linear.json and 20260616_004306_agent_gbdt.json authored_features_used lists contain only the 4 morphological measurements plus derived ratio/product features — species is absent from both. Leakage risk correctly mitigated.

suggestions.suggestion: The cv_holdout calibration check fires because floor_self_reported=0.0833 is used as relative denominator, but this floor is anomalously low. Record a proper random-baseline cv_score (0.333 for balanced 3-class) in model_selection.json so the 8% relative threshold uses a meaningful denominator.
suggestions.implementation_hint: In model_selection.json, add a 'random_baseline_cv_score' field computed as 1/n_classes for balanced classification; have the calibration check prefer this over floor_self_reported when available.

suggestions.suggestion: Two folds of 5 score perfect 1.0 for the linear specialist. If a round 2 runs, increase SGD alpha from 0.01 to 0.05-0.1 or add stronger l1 penalty to reduce fold-level overfit and tighten OOF-holdout gap.
suggestions.implementation_hint: In linear specialist hyperparameter grid, add alpha values [0.05, 0.1, 0.5] alongside current 0.01; select by mean OOF with lower variance (cv_stability < 0.02 target).

notes: Overall PASS with one medium WARN on cv_holdout calibration (gap 12.7% relative to true 3-class random baseline, triggered by artificially low floor denominator). No structural leakage: species excluded from all feature sets. Predictions are valid, non-constant, class-balanced. Small dataset (120 rows) explains fold variance. No high overfitting risk detected.
